gap_or_question: The CCF High Level Requirements workbook contains two sheets with conflicting wording for the 2-year re-application rule. The main 'High Level Requirements' sheet states: 'No previous application has been funded within the last 2 years.' An earlier 'Table format' sheet in the same workbook states: 'No previous application has been submitted within the last 2 years.' Which wording reflects the actual policy -- is an applicant who was rejected (not funded) within the last 2 years eligible to re-apply, or not? The HLR document's own note claims the main sheet 'supersedes' the Table-format sheet, but that is the document author's editorial call, not a client confirmation, and the two readings produce materially different outcomes.
impact_or_notes: Highest-priority gap for this epic -- direct input to the eligibility pass/fail determination (REQ-9). Must be confirmed with Rachel Doyle before the eligibility rule is built or tested; the wrong reading risks wrongly admitting or rejecting applicants at scale, a fairness/regulatory exposure given the client's stated Senate-estimates concern.

gap_or_question: REQ-9's business rules set a binary application status (Pending Accepted / Pending Rejected) when eligibility is assessed, but neither REQ-9 nor REQ-10 requires the system to capture *why* -- which criterion passed or failed, or whether a pass was a standard pass versus a special-project exception override. Should the eligibility outcome store the specific criteria evaluated (or override basis) alongside the status?
impact_or_notes: This is the exact mechanism behind Rachel's stated pain point: outcomes are logged 'eligible' but without the reasoning. Blocks the audit-defensibility outcome in the approved vision statement and strategy.json's 'every funding decision leaves a record' principle.

gap_or_question: Per the logged client decision, defining what qualifies as a 'special project' is a client-owned policy decision (Rachel + Legal) and out of scope. Once that policy exists, what specific criteria fields and approval/rationale data does the enforcement/audit structure need to capture against each application?
impact_or_notes: Does not ask Salesforce to define the policy -- asks what shape it will take so the data model and approval workflow can be designed. Until the client supplies a draft criteria structure, this piece of E02 can only be built as a generic, configurable override mechanism.

gap_or_question: The 2-year re-application check and the 'previous audit report submitted if previously successful' check both depend on correctly identifying an applicant's prior case history, but case-to-Account/Contact linking (REQ-8, E01) is a manual, non-deterministic CML process. If a repeat applicant links to a new/different record, will the 2-year and audit-history checks silently miss their prior case?
impact_or_notes: A false negative lets an ineligible re-application through undetected; a false positive wrongly blocks an eligible one. The same entity-name-mismatch data-quality risk already documented in disbursement plausibly applies here.

gap_or_question: The 2km-of-asset check runs today as a manual lookup against a separate mapping tool, causing ~40% of eligibility disputes. If moved into the CRM, should it be a native Salesforce geolocation/DISTANCE radius check, a true polygon/boundary-layer integration reflecting the actual shape of a substation or transmission corridor, or left as an external manual check?
impact_or_notes: Architecture fork -- central-KB checked (doc_search, Platform-filtered). [KA-14019] confirms native GEOLOCATION/DISTANCE radius queries exist, but no atom addresses a Geoscape-specific integration or true polygon/corridor boundary pattern. The point-vs-polygon precision question stays unresolved; recommend a targeted follow-up KB/architecture query at design time.

gap_or_question: REQ-9's five eligibility criteria are framed as the system 'shall support assessment... and flag if criteria are not met' -- not that it determines each automatically. Which criteria are system-determined versus a manual CML judgment call the system merely records, and for criterion 4 ('other required funding confirmed'), what counts as evidence?
impact_or_notes: Changes the build significantly -- a system-determined criterion needs a data source and rule; a judgment criterion only needs a capture field plus (per G0202) a reason/basis field.

gap_or_question: N/A -- risk framing, not a question requiring a client decision at this stage.
impact_or_notes: The current manual 2km check already produces ~40% of eligibility disputes at ~400 applications/year, with the board approving growth to ~1,000/year and no stated CML headcount change. Without a CRM-native resolution (G0205), dispute volume and CML workload should scale at least linearly, compounding an already-strained team.

gap_or_question: Geoscape has been assumed as the mapping/GIS tool CMLs use for the 2km check, based on the Org Health Assessment confirming it as an existing org-wide integration and the client's 'likely' confirmation during the strategy session -- not independently verified against what the CMLs actually use day-to-day.
impact_or_notes: Low effort, high value to close before design -- a brief confirmation with a CML avoids designing an integration against the wrong tool. Already carried as an [assumption:...] tag on epic E02; this formalizes it for tracking and feeds the G0205 architecture decision.

gap_or_question: If the 2km boundary check and special-project exception move into system-enforced rules, who owns keeping the underlying reference data current -- the asset/boundary geospatial data, and separately any criteria/reference data behind the special-project policy once it exists?
impact_or_notes: Buyer-facing governance question, not a mandate -- worth surfacing given the Org Health Assessment already flagged the absence of a Center of Excellence or Design Authority. Stale boundary data would directly reproduce the dispute problem this engagement is meant to fix.

gap_or_question: Should applicants get a clearer, self-service signal about the 2km rule before or at the point an EOI is rejected on eligibility -- e.g. an estimated distance-to-asset at submission, or a clearer rejection explanation -- rather than only finding out after manual CML review?
impact_or_notes: Buyer-facing experience-design question. Discovery attributes 40% of eligibility disputes to the 2km line specifically, described as a transparency/communication gap as much as a data gap. Worth asking whether the client wants this in scope or considers it a conscious deferral.

gap_or_question: HLR REQ-2 specifies that EOIs submitted via email are handled by an automated reply redirecting the sender to the public web form -- implying no case is created from the email itself. The discovery interview describes exactly this gap as the source of lost applications and two incidents that reached journalists. If REQ-2 is implemented literally, a sender who doesn't act on the redirect still leaves no record that an application attempt was ever made.
impact_or_notes: This is the core problem this epic exists to fix. Needs explicit resolution before design: should every inbound email create a system-of-record case automatically via Email-to-Case, with the redirect-to-web-form as a courtesy follow-up rather than the only response? Highest-priority gap in this epic.

gap_or_question: The exact automation mechanics behind the ~60% of EOIs submitted via the public web form are undocumented. Two different standard Salesforce patterns fit the description with different downstream consequences for attachments, multi-stage form state, and the reviewer workspace needed in E03/E04.
impact_or_notes: Architecture fork, central-KB checked: [KA-3884] confirms Web-to-Case as the generic bridge (simple, single-submission, no native multi-stage support). [KA-9719] confirms Form Framework (Nonprofit Cloud for Grantmaking / Public Sector) as purpose-built for multiphase applications with a consolidated reviewer workspace -- a better structural fit given the two-stage design and E04's panel-review needs. Needs an explicit design decision, not a default.

gap_or_question: None of REQ-1 through REQ-8 define a monitoring/alerting mechanism for the specific failure mode behind the two journalist-escalation incidents: an application arrives but no case is ever created, so it simply disappears.
impact_or_notes: Without an explicit 'did every inbound application produce a case' safety net, the rebuild risks looking complete on paper while leaving the actual reputational exposure unaddressed.

gap_or_question: HLR REQ-3 states the system 'should' enable attachments 'if required' at EOI stage. The actual EOI PDF form explicitly states: 'No attachments are required at this stage.' Confirmed by reading the source form directly, not just the HLR text.
impact_or_notes: Need to confirm whether REQ-3 is legacy/aspirational language to drop, or whether the client intends to change the EOI form to allow optional attachments. Low effort to resolve, but a direct textual conflict between two source documents.

gap_or_question: REQ-5 says the system 'shall apply case management rules and assign the case to Community Marketing Lead (CML)' (singular), but there are 4 CMLs covering an 'enormous' territory, and today's nominally geography-based routing is really ad hoc workload balancing, not a defined rule.
impact_or_notes: Architecture fork, central-KB checked: [KA-3975] confirms Case Assignment Rules (static, criteria-based, one active rule). [KA-4377] confirms Omni-Channel capacity/presence-based routing, which better matches the 'workload balancing' reality, especially given seasonal spikes that already pushed 2 of 4 CMLs onto medical leave. Needs an explicit design decision on static rules vs. capacity-aware routing.

gap_or_question: REQ-6/REQ-7 assume reliable email threading between reviewer, applicant, and the originating case. This is well-defined for Email-to-Case cases, but if G0102 resolves toward a non-email intake path, it's unaddressed whether follow-up replies will auto-attach to the correct case.
impact_or_notes: [extends: KA-3884 -- Email-to-Case threading is documented for email-originated cases; behavior for non-email-originated cases is outside that atom's scope and needs explicit design.] Left unresolved, REQ-6/7 risk silently failing for any case not created by email.

gap_or_question: No requirement addresses de-duplication across intake channels. The same applicant can submit via the web form and also email Rachel directly or someone met at a community forum for the same project, triggering two separate case-creation paths.
impact_or_notes: Without a defined match/merge rule across channels, this risks duplicate cases for the same application, double-counting volume, and confusing CMLs during triage -- compounding rather than fixing the current chaos.

gap_or_question: REQ-8 ('aid the CML to manually link a case to an existing or new account/contact via suggested matches') does not specify the matching mechanism, and it needs to work consistently across both intake channels.
impact_or_notes: Central-KB checked: the only grounded reference, [KA-3868] (Flow template matching on the case's Web Email field), is scoped to Email-to-Case-originated cases with no documented equivalent for web-form-originated cases. [KA-5005] confirms standard duplicate matching considers only a Contact's primary Account, which may under-match a repeat applicant organisation. Needs an explicit matching-rule design covering both channels.

gap_or_question: If case-creation automation is scoped primarily to the ~60% web-form path, the ~40% email path -- the actual source of both journalist-escalation incidents -- may remain manual and under-addressed.
impact_or_notes: The business case for this epic rests heavily on closing the lost-application/reputational-risk gap, which per the interview lives disproportionately in the email channel. Scope should explicitly commit to (or consciously defer) automating the email path, not just the higher-volume web path.

gap_or_question: Whatever triage/routing mechanism this epic lands on (see G0105) needs to hold up under seasonal spike volume, not just average throughput -- and the board has approved growth to ~1,000 applications/year by 2028.
impact_or_notes: A routing design that works at today's average volume but doesn't account for spike concentration risks reproducing the exact staff-strain failure this engagement is meant to prevent. Worth an explicit peak-week load assumption in design.

gap_or_question: Experience-design question: the EOI web form is the primary public-facing entry point for a growing, diverse applicant base under real public/reputational scrutiny. No UX research, accessibility review, or content design work is currently scoped for this form or the email-to-web-form redirect path.
impact_or_notes: Does the client's own team own usability/accessibility review for this form, or should it be scoped as dedicated experience-design work? A signal to surface as a buyer-facing question, not a mandate to add scope.

gap_or_question: Governance question: intake automation (web-form config, email routing, case assignment/routing rules, duplicate-matching) spans Comms and Platform administration, in an org already flagged as lacking a Center of Excellence or Design Authority. No requirement names who owns ongoing configuration of these rules post-go-live.
impact_or_notes: Absent clear ownership, intake automation risks degrading over time the same way the current manual process did -- a buyer-facing coverage question, not an assumed role.

gap_or_question: This epic's description ('via the public web form or email') is read as meaning both channels remain permanent intake paths going forward. REQ-2's redirect-only behavior for email suggests the client's documented intent may actually be to phase out email as a direct intake channel over time.
impact_or_notes: [assumption: both channels stay permanent -- confirm with Rachel/Comms before committing build effort specifically to hardening the email intake path, since that effort is wasted if the real intent is to deprecate email intake in favor of the web form.]

gap_or_question: The EOI form (CCF-EOI-v1) publishes hard, round-based Full Application deadlines (31 Jan for the Summer round, 31 July for Winter), but neither REQ-13 nor REQ-14 defines any deadline-driven reminder or escalation. The known pain point -- CML turnaround 'three days to never' with manual chasing -- is exactly what this epic exists to fix, and the deadline to nudge against already exists in print.
impact_or_notes: Automation gap against an existing published rule, not a new policy decision. Recommend an automated reminder cadence plus a defined behavior for applications that miss the deadline. Directly reduces CML manual-chasing load.

gap_or_question: The Full Application form explicitly states 'This form cannot be saved partially.' But it's a long, document-heavy, multi-section form -- exactly the shape Salesforce's standard Public Sector Grantmaking pattern builds save-for-later support for [KA-9509].
impact_or_notes: Building to the stated 'no partial save' rule forgoes a native capability that reduces abandonment; silently adding save-for-later contradicts the client's own form copy and may have been intentional policy. Confirm with Rachel/Legal before this becomes a build default either way.

gap_or_question: Both the EOI and Full Application carry real conditional-field logic (GST status branching, amount-changed-since-EOI, quote-sum-vs-requested-amount reconciliation) with no corresponding business rule in the HLR. The standard build pattern for this branching is OmniScript dynamic conditional questions [KA-9655].
impact_or_notes: Someone needs to decide validation behavior: does the system block submission if quotes don't sum to the stated amount, or just flag it for CML review? Left undefined, this becomes an inconsistent manual check per CML.

gap_or_question: Full Application Q8/9 anticipates the requested amount changing since EOI. If an amount crosses the $50K panel-review threshold between EOI and Full Application, no rule exists for whether that re-routes the application onto a different review track in E04.
impact_or_notes: Without a rule, an application could be reviewed at the wrong governance level relative to its actual dollar value -- a direct miss against the engagement's defensibility goal.

gap_or_question: The Full Application mandates a co-applicant's personal details, with a declaration that they are 'aware they are part of the application' -- attested only by the primary applicant, never confirmed independently. REQ-14 doesn't mention a co-applicant at all.
impact_or_notes: Northwind Grid would be capturing a non-submitting individual's personal contact details on an unverified third-party attestation -- a real privacy exposure for a regulator-scrutinized utility. Recommend confirming whether a direct consent step to the co-applicant is in scope.

gap_or_question: Nothing addresses whether the co-applicant should be matched/deduplicated against existing Contacts like the primary applicant (REQ-8), created fresh every time, or stored as flat text fields.
impact_or_notes: Without a decision, the same recurring office-bearer could end up as a disconnected duplicate Contact across years of applications -- undermining the defensible-record-keeping goal this engagement is built around.

gap_or_question: Full Application Q1/Q2 require an exact 8-digit reference and matching email to link back to the EOI/Case. Neither REQ-13 nor REQ-14 defines what happens on a mismatch -- blocked submission, failed case link, or manual CML triage?
impact_or_notes: An unhandled mismatch risks recreating the 'lost application' scenario that has already reached journalists twice -- a small but load-bearing validation rule to leave undefined.

gap_or_question: Full Application Q7 notes distance will be 'verified during shortlisting' (an E04 activity), implying the EOI-stage 2km eligibility pass is provisional. Nothing states whether a Full Application can be rejected at shortlisting for failing the 2km check after clearing EOI eligibility, or how that reversal is logged.
impact_or_notes: Relevant to both E02 and E04. Given 40% of eligibility disputes already sit on this exact line, an undefined re-verification/reversal path is a likely source of disputes and inconsistent CML handling.

gap_or_question: Full Application Q13 offers volunteer support from Northwind Grid staff in five metro regions -- a stub with a real downstream business process (coordinating volunteering days) and zero system support defined anywhere in the HLR.
impact_or_notes: Confirm whether this needs CRM-side tracking/routing (e.g. a task to a volunteering coordinator), or is handled entirely outside Salesforce. Left unaddressed, these responses will likely go uncollected.

gap_or_question: Full Application Q14/15 ask about planned promotional activity. Nothing describes what the CML, panel, or Comms team does with this answer -- feeds strategic-criteria scoring in E04, triggers a co-marketing conversation, or purely informational?
impact_or_notes: Confirm intended use before deciding whether this needs a structured field, a workflow trigger, or a scoring linkage into E04.

gap_or_question: The Full Application tells applicants their submission will be evaluated against strategic criteria (diversity, lower socio-economic areas, environmental benefit, low-carbon support) -- but no structured field captures these at intake; panel members must infer them from free-text narrative.
impact_or_notes: Directly undercuts E04's panel-scoring-integrity goal -- a tamper-evident score is only as defensible as the structured basis behind it. Decide whether any criteria should become explicit, scorable fields rather than narrative inference.

gap_or_question: Section 8 requires both the primary applicant's and co-applicant's signature/date -- a two-party e-signature/attestation workflow. Central-KB atoms found for e-signature/consent patterns are scoped to Financial Services, Health/Life Sciences, Consumer Goods, and Field Service -- none target Public Sector or Grantmaking.
impact_or_notes: Ungrounded for the Public Sector/Grantmaking context specifically. Flag before committing to a build approach (native e-signature product vs. a simple dual-checkbox/typed-name attestation) -- don't default to the nearest off-cloud pattern.

gap_or_question: The document checklist requires either two competitive quotes or documented reasoning for one, plus optional letters of support and an open 'other' category. REQ-15 only says the system shall 'support uploading and storing' documentation -- the required/optional mix and the either/or quotes-vs-justification condition aren't specified.
impact_or_notes: No defined rule for what blocks submission versus what's merely requested but not enforced -- left to the build team to guess, or CMLs to manually catch after the fact.

gap_or_question: Experience-design signal: this single form packs real UX complexity (GST-conditional fields, amount-changed branch, city-conditional volunteer question, mandatory co-applicant sub-section, conditional document checklist, no-partial-save constraint). Is a dedicated UX/content-design pass in scope, or is standard Form Framework/OmniScript configuration assumed sufficient?
impact_or_notes: The current PDF reads as a static, page-by-page form, not a designed digital flow -- that gap compounds as volume scales toward 1,000/year. A signal to raise with the client, not a mandate to add a UX epic.

gap_or_question: Governance signal: capturing a non-submitting co-applicant's PII (G0305), and any change to the 'cannot save partially' rule (G0302), are data-handling/consent and form-policy decisions. Does Northwind Grid have, or need, a data-stewardship owner who signs off on third-party PII capture rules and form-behavior changes before they ship?
impact_or_notes: A concrete instance of the governance absence already flagged platform-wide (Org Health Assessment: no CoE/Design Authority) -- worth naming explicitly here rather than letting it surface only as an abstract platform-level finding.

gap_or_question: The discovery interview describes the approval panel meeting quarterly; the CCF Expression of Interest application form explicitly states the panel meets twice a year (March, September). The client has indicated the form is likely accurate but this has not been formally confirmed. Can Northwind Grid confirm the actual panel cadence before SLA timers and alert cadence are locked in?
impact_or_notes: Directly affects batch size per cycle, prep-pack generation timing, reviewer-reminder cadence, and the licensing consumption model for external panellists (see G0408). Quarterly vs. twice-yearly roughly doubles expected caseload per cycle.

gap_or_question: Neither the HLR nor the interview defines what dollar figure the $50K panel-routing threshold is measured against -- the amount requested at full application, a CML/HoC-adjusted amount, or (for staged grants) the full agreement value vs. a single stage?
impact_or_notes: Without a defined basis, routing automation can't be built deterministically -- e.g. a $45K request amended to $55K, or a $200K grant split into four $50K stages, both create ambiguous routing outcomes. [assumption: requested amount at full-application submission, pending client confirmation].

gap_or_question: REQ-16's alert to the Head of Communications is already too noisy per Rachel's own account (~40/week, binary). Within the under-$50K track, which applications genuinely need Rachel's direct review versus the CML's alone, and on what criteria?
impact_or_notes: Without a defined filtering rule, this epic risks rebuilding the same binary, unfiltered alert Rachel explicitly flagged as broken. A scope decision, not a Salesforce capability gap.

gap_or_question: Does the under-$50K track use the same shortlist/not-shortlist mechanism (REQ-19) before CML/HoC makes the final accept/reject call, or does it skip shortlisting entirely and go straight to a CML/HoC accept-reject decision?
impact_or_notes: Determines whether the under- and over-$50K tracks share one status/stage model or need two distinct ones. Risks inconsistent case-status transitions that would break the single-case-history reporting Rachel's team needs for MP/ministerial briefing notes.

gap_or_question: REQ-21 states each panel member scores an application 'out of ten across five criteria' but neither source names what those five criteria actually are. What are they, and are they fixed program-wide or do they vary by grant type/round?
impact_or_notes: Foundational data-model input -- the scoring object/fields can't be built without it. Flagging rather than inventing placeholder criteria.

gap_or_question: REQ-21's business rule says panel scores 'remain editable until accepted or rejected' -- but panel-scoring integrity (an immutable, tamper-evident record) is Rachel's #3 stated priority, precisely because today's open-editability rule enables undetected post-meeting score changes. Should the editability window be shortened, or does the business need post-meeting edits with only logging added?
impact_or_notes: Architecture fork, KB-checked: Field History Tracking/Field Audit Trail [KA-11166/KA-11334/KA-9960/KA-11335] logs changes but does not block an edit -- a log, not a lock. True prevention needs a separate record-lock mechanism (validation rule or approval-process pattern, [KA-9640]). REQ-21 as written and Rachel's stated priority are in direct tension; which governs is a client decision.

gap_or_question: The 5 external panellists lack Salesforce logins and score via spreadsheet with manual transcription. Does Northwind Grid want to adopt the standard Experience Cloud 'Grantmaking' site pattern for this (requiring new licenses to be procured/budgeted), or is there a reason to keep external panellists off the platform entirely?
impact_or_notes: Architecture fork, grounded: [KA-9728/KA-9719/KA-9511] confirm the Grantmaking Experience Cloud template explicitly supports external reviewers; [KA-10444] confirms login-based licensing suited to infrequent panellists; [KA-0417] is internal-opinion, labeled as such. This is a real license cost not yet in any budget conversation -- needs client sign-off before being treated as committed scope.

gap_or_question: The research finding that login-based licensing suits panellists 'who review only twice a year' assumes the twice-yearly cadence from the form, not the quarterly cadence from the interview. If G0401 resolves to quarterly, does the licensing cost-efficiency case still hold?
impact_or_notes: Downstream of G0401 -- a distinct consequence (licensing cost model) rather than just an SLA-timer question. [assumption: twice-yearly cadence, per the application form -- carries through to G0407 until G0401 is resolved].

gap_or_question: Is each panellist's score visible to other panellists before or during the panel discussion, or only revealed/collated at the meeting? Real-time visibility could itself invite anchoring or pressure to conform, separate from the post-meeting editability issue in G0406.
impact_or_notes: Not addressed in either source document. Affects both the review-workspace UX and the integrity design -- worth resolving alongside G0406 since both bear on panel-scoring integrity.

gap_or_question: The interview describes a 15-application prep pack sent to panellists in advance of each meeting; REQ-22 only allows assessors to generically 'generate a report or filter applications.' Should pack generation and distribution to all 11 panellists (including the 5 external) be explicitly in scope for this epic?
impact_or_notes: If pack generation/distribution isn't explicitly scoped, the external-panellist-workspace fix (G0407) could land without actually removing the manual prep-pack assembly step that drives most of the cited 40 hrs/year cost.

gap_or_question: N/A -- risk framing. At the board-approved target of ~1,000 applications/year, panel-eligible volume scales proportionally -- each panel cycle could face 2-3x today's per-meeting caseload. Does the panel review workspace and scoring UX need to be explicitly designed/tested for that higher volume now?
impact_or_notes: The epic description as given doesn't size for scale. This epic's acceptance criteria should state what volume it's actually built and tested against.

gap_or_question: No turnaround SLA is defined for the CML/Head-of-Communications assessment stage on under-$50K applications. Should this stage carry a target turnaround, and if so, should missing it trigger an escalation alert?
impact_or_notes: Without a defined SLA, there's no basis for designing an escalation/reminder mechanism for this stage.

gap_or_question: REQ-25 states rejected applicants are notified 'after all applications are processed' -- unlike REQ-24's approval notification, which fires per-decision. Is batching rejection notices until the full cycle completes intentional (e.g. to avoid comparative appeals), or should rejections notify individually like approvals?
impact_or_notes: Affects notification-automation design and applicant experience -- a rejected applicant from early in a cycle waits for the whole batch to clear before hearing anything, which may itself generate the MP-escalation pattern Rachel described.

gap_or_question: The 11-person panel includes 6 internal roles alongside 5 external members deciding on grants that can run into the millions, yet neither document addresses conflict-of-interest handling. Does Northwind Grid have an existing COI policy for the panel that Salesforce should enforce, or does this need to be defined as part of this engagement?
impact_or_notes: Governance discipline gap, a signal not a mandate. Given the regulator scrutiny and Senate-estimates exposure already on record for this program, an undefined COI process on a panel this consequential is a material gap worth surfacing.

gap_or_question: The external-panellist review workspace is a net-new portal experience for people who have never used Salesforce and engage with it only a few times a year. Has any user research, usability testing, or onboarding plan been scoped for these 5 external users?
impact_or_notes: Experience-design discipline gap, a signal not a mandate. Infrequent, non-technical external users are exactly the population most likely to abandon or misuse a portal without onboarding design, undercutting the 40 hrs/year efficiency gain this capability is meant to deliver.

gap_or_question: Neither document defines how a split or contentious panel vote is resolved -- is a simple majority sufficient, does Rachel hold a tie-breaking or veto role, and is there any appeal mechanism distinct from the MP/ministerial escalation path?
impact_or_notes: Related to but distinct from G0406 (score mutability) -- this is about the decision rule itself. Given Rachel's account of 'gaming' suspicion around contentious outcomes, an undefined decision rule compounds the same fairness/defensibility exposure the regulator already targets.

gap_or_question: HLR REQ-29 implies a direct Salesforce-to-gateway integration for payment release and settlement acknowledgement. The discovery interview describes a different topology -- payment failures happen entirely inside AP's SAP/EFT-gateway world and never reach Salesforce at all. Which integration topology is real?
impact_or_notes: Load-bearing to the whole epic's architecture. If Salesforce only talks to SAP (and SAP talks to the gateway), the 'Funded - Payment Held' fix depends entirely on SAP relaying gateway outcomes back, a different integration/SLA/ownership story than Salesforce-to-gateway directly. Confirm with Rachel/AP before design.

gap_or_question: Rachel's #1 priority is 'validated' entity-name and bank-detail exchange with SAP, but no HLR requirement specifies an actual validation step (e.g. an ABN/ABR registry lookup) that would catch the entity-name mismatch before it reaches AP -- today the mismatch is caught downstream, after the applicant has already been told they're approved.
impact_or_notes: Without an explicit pre-validation requirement, 'eliminate duplicate vendor setup' risks being built as a straight data-passthrough that still inherits the ~1/3 mismatch-bounce rate. No central-KB atom addressed ABN/ABR validation specifically -- flag as a capability gap requiring a concrete validation ruleset before this can be sized or built.

gap_or_question: N/A -- architecture risk framing. Which system is master for vendor/payee identity (Salesforce or SAP), and whether a simple validation callout or dedicated MDM tooling is needed, is not resolved by any source document and is not a decision Salesforce discovery can make unilaterally.
impact_or_notes: Central-KB checked: [KA-9480/KA-9482] ground the general shape (Salesforce generates a payment instruction, sends via integration, stores ERP external ID back), explicitly not prescribing middleware. [KA-0012/KA-0138] ground the sync/async selection matrix. [KA-0039] grounds the MuleSoft-vs-Informatica app-connectivity-vs-MDM split but doesn't resolve vendor-identity ownership for this scenario. Recommend a targeted design-stage query before committing to a pattern.

gap_or_question: The AP-owned EFT/payment gateway platform is never named in any source document -- already an open question in the Discovery Brief, but it specifically blocks scoping REQ-29/REQ-30 for this epic.
impact_or_notes: Cannot scope the settlement/failure-outcome integration without knowing what the gateway is and what it can expose. A client fact-gathering gap, not resolvable via KB search -- needs direct confirmation from AP.

gap_or_question: REQ-30 requires receiving/recording Settled/Failed/Pending outcomes but specifies no mechanism -- webhook/callback push, scheduled polling, or manual re-keying. The choice materially changes the architecture and timeliness of the 'Funded - Payment Held' fix.
impact_or_notes: [KA-13702] grounds the sync-vs-async decision framework generally. Given G0504 (gateway identity unknown), it is not yet knowable which model fits. Flag pending G0504's resolution.

gap_or_question: REQ-30's business rule says a failed disbursement should 'flag the case for CML follow-up' but specifies no notification mechanism, no escalation if the CML doesn't act, and no visibility for Rachel, who explicitly wants to stop learning about failures only when the recipient calls three weeks later.
impact_or_notes: Without a defined alert/escalation workflow, the new status could exist in the data model but still go unnoticed. Should mirror the escalation design pattern Rachel wants for audit tracking (CML then her, on a timer) rather than being designed independently.

gap_or_question: REQ-31 covers the staged-disbursement data model going forward but says nothing about migrating the ~20 existing grants tracked entirely on the PA's spreadsheet, or about due-date reminders/alerts for upcoming milestones -- the single point of failure Rachel flagged unprompted.
impact_or_notes: Treat as two sub-gaps: migration scope (one-time, necessary to actually retire the spreadsheet) and milestone-reminder automation (ongoing, a standard scheduled Flow capability, no KB grounding needed).

gap_or_question: No requirement defines what happens operationally after a disbursement is flagged 'Funded - Payment Held' -- does the CML correct details and the system auto-retries, is a new request required, is there a retry cap, and does a corrected retry need re-approval from Legal/panel for grants that originally required it?
impact_or_notes: Without this, the new status is diagnostic only and doesn't close the loop on getting the recipient paid, leaving the 6-8 week large-grant cycle exposed to the same friction on retry. Needs a client decision on the retry/resubmission workflow.

gap_or_question: REQ-28's 'every disbursement must have a matching payable, no back-door payments' implies a strict one-to-one constraint, but no requirement addresses a timeout/retry on the Salesforce-to-SAP push -- is there a double-payment risk if a resend creates two payables for one disbursement record, and what idempotency safeguard is required?
impact_or_notes: [KA-0039] notes MuleSoft's role in transactional reliability generally, grounding why idempotency matters, but supplies no Northwind-specific requirement. No explicit idempotency/duplicate-payable requirement exists -- recommend adding one given this handles real money.

gap_or_question: REQ-28 requires the payment request to include GL/cost-centre coding, but doesn't specify whether Salesforce derives/maps this coding (requiring a grant-type-to-GL-code mapping maintained in Salesforce) or AP appends it manually after receiving the request.
impact_or_notes: Changes build scope materially -- a Salesforce-side GL-mapping table versus a pass-through field. Needs confirmation with Finance/AP; a scope-definition question, not an architecture fork.

gap_or_question: REQ-27 states payment details are 'captured once and re-used for any staged or split disbursements' -- but staged grants run over a multi-year schedule during which bank/entity details could legitimately change, with no requirement for re-validation or staleness-checking before a later-stage payment.
impact_or_notes: Risk of releasing a later-stage payment against stale bank details with no system prompt to re-confirm -- a direct financial-control gap on grants running into six figures. Worth surfacing to Rachel/Finance as a control to consider, without inflating scope unilaterally.

gap_or_question: No data-residency or PII-handling requirement is defined anywhere for the bank account numbers, ABNs, and tax reference numbers this epic captures and transmits -- flagged generally in the Discovery Brief, but directly load-bearing here since this epic is where that data is captured, stored, and transmitted.
impact_or_notes: The most sensitive payload in the entire CCF rebuild; absence of a stated residency/encryption/masking requirement should be closed before field-level design. A client policy question, confirm with Northwind Grid's security/compliance function.

gap_or_question: The interview describes Legal reviewing ASIC/ABN documentation and gating grants over $100K, with a 5-day SLA routinely missed -- but no corresponding requirement exists in the HLR. Should this be modeled as a case stage/approval step inside Salesforce with SLA visibility, or does it remain an entirely manual, off-system gate?
impact_or_notes: If Legal's review stays off-system, the epic can't report on or alert against the single biggest named contributor to the 6-8 week disbursement cycle on exactly the grants where speed matters most. Needs a scope decision from the client.

gap_or_question: The disbursement chain spans three organizationally separate teams (CRM/Comms, Finance/AP, Legal) and no source document names a single accountable owner for the end-to-end disbursement SLA, for remediating a failed payment, or for vendor-record data quality once it exists in both systems. Who owns the cross-team disbursement process once this is built?
impact_or_notes: Mirrors the exact pattern that already causes the current 6-8 week cycle time. Rebuilding without resolving ownership risks reproducing the same cross-team friction in a more automated form -- a client operating-model decision, not a Salesforce build item.

gap_or_question: The engagement framing describes the vendor-integration fix as Salesforce and SAP 'exchanging validated' data as if the validation ruleset were already understood, but no document defines what 'validated' means operationally (exact match vs. fuzzy threshold, live API callout vs. batch check).
impact_or_notes: [assumption: a concrete validation ruleset will be defined and confirmed with the client before design] -- the same underlying gap as G0502 viewed from the angle that the engagement narrative already assumes a solution exists. Easy for this to slip through requirements unexamined given how confidently the three priorities are framed.

gap_or_question: REQ-34 (HLR) documents only a single escalation tier (an alert to the CML). The discovery interview and the epic description both describe three tiers -- chase the recipient, escalate to a CML, then escalate to the Head of Communications if it goes past overdue. The HLR is silent on recipient-chasing and the second escalation tier.
impact_or_notes: Building to REQ-34 literally would ship a single CML-only alert with no recipient chasing and no Head-of-Comms escalation -- missing two of the three mechanisms the epic claims to deliver. Needs explicit reconciliation: confirm the three-tier model before design, and update the HLR record so it's not relied on as complete.

gap_or_question: Neither REQ-32 nor any other HLR requirement specifies how an audit report actually gets into Salesforce as a trackable record. Today recipients email receipts/PDFs to a shared inbox or directly to a team member, with ad hoc storage. Is a structured intake mechanism in scope for this epic, or is E06 only the tracking/chasing/escalation layer that assumes a report lands on the case 'somehow'?
impact_or_notes: This is the actual root cause behind the ~20% late/missing rate -- not the absence of a reminder, but the absence of a reliable path for the report to arrive and attach. If E06 only builds chasing/escalation logic and leaves intake as-is, the system will faithfully escalate on reports that were actually submitted but lost. Scope must explicitly state whether intake is in or out.

gap_or_question: REQ-33's rule says the case closes when the audit report is 'submitted and marked as complete (ticked)' -- no source defines who ticks it, against what evidentiary standard, or whether there's a review step. Simple receipts for small grants vs. outcomes/impact reports for larger ones implies 'complete' means something different by grant size, but no criteria are given for either.
impact_or_notes: Without a defined reviewer and criteria, 'marked complete' is an unaudited checkbox, reproducing the governance weakness already flagged for panel scoring and special-project overrides. Given the regulator has asked for 'evidence of monitoring,' an undefined completion standard is itself a compliance exposure, not just a UX detail.

gap_or_question: No source discusses whether the 5 years of pre-existing audit-report status data (the subject of the Senior Advisor's 3-day manual spreadsheet exercise, which still had unexplained gaps) needs to be migrated/backfilled into whatever new tracking mechanism E06 builds.
impact_or_notes: If historical in-flight grants aren't backfilled with their actual funded-date and audit status, the new automated clock starts blind on every grant already in flight -- firing false alerts or silently failing to track. Directly undermines the goal of giving Rachel a defensible answer to the regulator, since their concern is specifically about the historical record, not just new grants.

gap_or_question: Buyer-facing governance question: who formally owns the decision to mark an audit report 'complete,' and what specific time/criteria threshold triggers escalation from the CML tier to the Head of Communications tier? Today both are informal, and 'past overdue' is undefined.
impact_or_notes: The same category of governance gap Rachel named for special-project exceptions and panel scoring -- a decision point with no documented owner or criteria creates the identical defensibility problem the regulator and a potential Senate estimates question already target.

gap_or_question: For the ~20 staged/milestone grants, does the 2-year post-funding audit clock start at the first disbursement (signing) or the final/completion disbursement? REQ-34's 'waits 2 years once a fund is processed' is ambiguous when 'processed' happens in three separate events over time.
impact_or_notes: Getting this wrong either starts the clock too early or misses the regulator's 2-year window on large grants, the ones most likely to draw scrutiny. Direct dependency on E05's staged-disbursement tracking -- the two epics need a shared answer on what event starts the audit-tracking clock.

gap_or_question: No requirement captures what evidentiary type of audit report is expected per grant (receipts vs. outcomes report), or where that expectation is set and recorded so an automated chase message can tell the recipient what's required.
impact_or_notes: An automated chase that just says 'submit your audit report' without specifying what's required is less useful than today's manual process. Needs a field/rule tying grant size/type to the expected report type, set at award time.

gap_or_question: Chasing and first-tier escalation go to 'a CML,' but CMLs are workload-balanced across an enormous territory and two of four were on medical leave during last year's spike. No source addresses what happens to a grant's audit-tracking responsibility if the originally assigned CML leaves, transfers, or is on extended leave before the 2-year mark.
impact_or_notes: Without a reassignment rule, a long-dated obligation risks silently stalling exactly the way today's PA-dependent process already does. Recommend tying the chase/escalation owner to a role or queue rather than a named CML record.

gap_or_question: The epic description implicitly assumes a report, once it arrives, reliably attaches to the correct case/grant record. Today that's explicitly not true. If E06 is scoped as tracking/chasing/escalation only and not intake (per G0602), this assumption may not hold at go-live.
impact_or_notes: [assumption: storage reliability improves incidentally from E01-E05 case-management work; not confirmed as in scope anywhere] -- even if intake stays out of scope, this needs to be stated and accepted, or the same ~20%-type gap just relocates rather than closes.

gap_or_question: The org has no time-based automation wired to the Case object for a multi-year due-date clock with tiered escalation -- the HLR doesn't specify a mechanism, and today's enforcement is a human calendar reminder plus a manually-run monthly report.
impact_or_notes: Architecture fork for design, not yet resolved: SLA Policies/Entitlement Milestones [KA-4590/KA-4033] or Case Escalation Rules [KA-4456] are standard options; the central-KB Public Sector Grantmaking overview [KA-9728] separately confirms 'Manage Grant Recipient Progress Reports' as the grantmaking-specific pattern. No atom resolves which fits a 2-year horizon best -- flag for design to pick a mechanism rather than defaulting to a custom scheduled Flow/Apex batch.
